contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-eligibility-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-managed-payments-eligibility-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-eligibility.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/eligibility`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/eligibility, November describes Stripe's eligibility review for direct integrations in supported business locations. Connect platforms, Express accounts and platform-controlled accounts are excluded (new raw lines 9-68). On a Checkout Session or Payment Link, each product must be an eligible fully automated digital sale direct to the customer, with distribution rights and an eligible Product tax code assigned in the Dashboard or via API. Physical goods, professional services and live in-person events are excluded. If Stripe finds the product ineligible, the merchant bears indirect tax liability and must stop using Managed Payments for that product (old raw lines 70-102 and new raw lines 70-102). More than 195 customer countries and territories and the nine restrictions are separate from merchant domicile. Ongoing eligibility requires a low historical dispute rate and no prior risk issues. Stripe can refund within 60 days in certain cases and applies applicable consumer protections (new raw lines 185-209). November omits Gibraltar and Website Advertising, adds four AIaaS codes and excludes data brokering from four information-service codes (old raw lines 30-62, 113-121 and 166-171; new raw lines 31-61, 117-120 and 170-174). source-stripe-managed-payments-eligibility.md preserves much of the April outline but omits the review and direct sales/rights requirements and uses code ranges that are broader than the enumerated list. A listed country and tax code are inputs to eligibility review and do not prove approval, compliant coverage or payment success.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/eligibility, the substantive listing changes are 38 to 37 merchant-location entries with Gibraltar omitted, four AIaaS additions txcd_10105001, txcd_10105002, txcd_10105003 and txcd_10105004 for cloud-only or downloaded-plus-cloud and personal or business use, removal of the Website Advertising row txcd_10701000, and new data-brokering exclusions for txcd_10701400, txcd_10701401, txcd_10701410 and txcd_10701411 (old raw lines 30-69, 113-121 and 166-171; new raw lines 31-68, 117-120 and 170-174). The changelog dates the AIaaS addition to June 2. Preserve April's Gibraltar and Website Advertising entries and the changelog's separately dated 39-country April GA milestone in source-stripe-managed-payments-eligibility.md and reciprocal concept and changelog routes. The November tax-compliance page's GI entry is for cross-border customer tax coverage. The November changelog also omits Website Advertising from its September 2025 entry, while the April capture listed it there. Neither omission gives an effective change date or account-specific treatment. Buyer-to-customer terminology, Markdown layout and the dispute-rate hyperlink are presentational or navigational. Keep the per-Product Dashboard/API code and Checkout Session or Payment Link scope, the US-sales qualification for the relevant business/personal rows, and Stripe's conditional rather than automatic 60-day refund authority (new raw lines 70-102, 117-120 and 201-209). Both captures exclude live in-person events, as the mapped summary correctly says. The Managed Payments concept should qualify its broader live-event exclusion and point back to the exact audiovisual rows, which can cover digitally delivered live-event content (old raw lines 84-98, 149-151 and 172-174; new raw lines 84-98, 153-155 and 175-177). Check the delivery model, direct sale and distribution rights independently of the subject of the content. The general electronically supplied services code mentions minimal human involvement (old and new raw line 108). The separate fully automated requirement still excludes live human-delivered services. This distinction was present in both captures.
